newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Islamic banking seen booming in Bahrain.
newsitem.headline: Islamic banking seen booming in Bahrain.

text.p: Islamic banking is developing in Bahrain to cash in on growing demand by Moslems worldwide, a senior banker said on Tuesday.
"Of course Islamic banking is developing well in Bahrain," Ghazi Abdul-Jawad, general manager of the Gulf International Bank (GIB), told Reuters in an interview.
"Bahrain has strategically positioned itself to push Islamic banking forward, and there are many developments that are moving in tandem," he said.
Bahrain, which hosts 48 offshore banking units and several Islamic banks, is the Gulf's main financial and banking centre.
Abdul-Jawad said Bahrain Institute for Banking and Finance would launch a separate Islamic banking division in 1997.
He said the Accounting and Auditing Organisation for Islamic Financial Institutions concluded a meeting in Bahrain last week to push for standardised accounting principles for Islamic institutions.
"All of that is preparing very solid grounds to have Bahrain develop Islamic banking," he added.
Islamic banks do not deal in interest -- the core of the Western banking system -- as it is regarded by many Moslems as usury, banned under Islamic Sharia law.
Bankers say Islamic banks had become more popular among the world's one billion Moslems, but the more than 185 financial institutions face hurdles to lure more funds.

The banks, facing increasing competition from Western banks offering Islamic products, needed to educate more Moslems about their services, standardise their product and develop a sound legal framework in which to operate.
The Saudi-based International Association of Islamic Banks said last month Islamic financial institutions' assets had jumped 21 times in 10 years to around $166 billion in 1995.
Citicorp unit Citibank opened a new $20 million Islamic bank based in Bahrain in July.

First Islamic Investment Bank, formed by the Saudi Al Jomaih Group and the Cayman Islands-registered and Kuwaiti-owned Majestic Global Investments -- recently received a licence to open a $50 million Islamic Bank in Bahrain.
Arab Banking Corporation also plans to launch a new $100 million Islamic bank in the island in 1997.
